concepts.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
concepts.definition: Forces acting on a body may cancel or combine: equal and opposite forces balance to leave motion unchanged, while an unbalanced net force is needed to start motion, stop it, or change its speed or direction.
concepts.key_idea: No change without imbalance: motion changes only under a net force.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc106.txt sections on balanced and unbalanced forces

solution_steps.explain: Identify every push or pull with its direction.
Opposite forces subtract; same-side forces add.
Zero net force keeps motion unchanged; nonzero net force changes it.

concepts.title: Newton's Laws of Motion and Inertia
concepts.definition: Newton's first law states that a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts - the property of inertia, which depends on mass; the second law links force to the rate of change of momentum, giving force equals mass times acceleration.
concepts.key_idea: Inertia resists change; the second law measures the push needed as mass times acceleration.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc106.txt sections on Newton's laws and inertia

solution_steps.explain: The net force is the product of mass and acceleration.

concepts.title: Action-Reaction and Conservation of Momentum
concepts.definition: Forces come in pairs - every action has an equal and opposite reaction; in a system with no external force the total momentum stays conserved, which is why a gun recoils and rockets push forward by throwing gas backward.
concepts.key_idea: Push the world and it pushes back: paired forces and conserved momentum run the show.

solution_steps.explain: Name the two bodies exchanging the action-reaction forces.
Total momentum before equals total momentum after.
The recoil, rocket or swimmer moves as momentum balances.
